{{Short description|Sierpiński–Menger type of fractal}}
[[File:Moselycube1.gif|thumb|right|300px| Mosely snowflake formation during four recursion steps]]
[[File:Moselycube.gif|thumb|right|250px| Mosely snowflake (heavier) formation during four recursion steps]]
The '''Mosely snowflake''' (after [[Jeannine Mosely]]) is a [[Sierpinski sponge|Sierpiński]]–[[Menger sponge|Menger]] type of [[fractal]] obtained in two variants either by the operation opposite to creating the [[Menger sponge|Sierpiński-Menger snowflake]] or [[Cantor set|Cantor dust]] i.e. not by leaving but by removing eight of the smaller 1/3-scaled corner cubes and the central one from each cube left from the previous recursion (lighter) or by removing only corner cubes (heavier).<ref>Eric Baird, ''Alt.Fractals: A visual guide to fractal geometry and design'' (January 2011), pages 21 and 62-64. {{ISBN|9780955706837}}</ref> 

In one dimension this operation (i.e. the recursive removal of two side line segments) is trivial and converges only to single point. It resembles the original water [[snowflake]] of [[snow]]. By construction the Hausdorff dimension of the lighter snowflake is 

<math>d_H=\log_3 (27-9) = \ln 18 / \ln 3 \approx 2.630929</math>

and the heavier 

<math>d_H=\log_3 (27-8) = \ln 19 / \ln 3 \approx 2.680143</math>.
